proof_attempt_summary: D0 developed matched three-regime risk and honest-length orders, including the critical logarithmic converse; two independent maximality consults reported no false or laundered claim, and a scoped revision promoted the critical-modulus order and witness coefficient. D0.5 capped the package at subfield below field: redundant assumptions, closest-literature proof access, and practical interval informativeness remain unresolved. Formalization never began; no Lean module, type-checking, or axiom-clean certification is claimed, and the global critical constant remains open.
tldr: Conceptual \((1,1)\)-trimmed L-skewness is finite in the declared envelope even though ordinary means can diverge. For its causal arm contrast \(\theta\), the complete-class all-procedure absolute-risk and honest connected-interval frontiers are proved: \(n^{-1/2}\) below \(\beta=1/4\), \(\sqrt{\log(en)/n}\) at equality, and \(n^{-1/[2(3/4+\beta)]}\) above. The total mixed-stratum inverse-censor U-statistic estimator and public bias-plus-variance interval attain these orders for every integer sample size. Normalized same-class alternatives in the full event-and-censor experiment prove the converse. At critical censoring the complete-class Hellinger modulus has order \(\epsilon\sqrt{\log(1/\epsilon)}\); an explicit legal four-cell optimization gives the computable witness coefficient \(\sqrt{24\Gamma}\). Only its exact complete-class coefficient, limit existence and extremizers remain open. Identification is given by causal survival adjustment.
gap: Gaussian L-functional and ratio convergence, local regular-estimator information bounds, and second-order tail-extrapolation CLTs do not, from their inspected hypotheses, determine precision over the complete declared envelope. The unresolved object is the all-procedure observed-experiment frontier, especially its critical logarithmic converse and finite-sample honest length.
fill: The two frontier theorems pair a computable clipped procedure with same-class testing alternatives. Conditional overlap bounds, random-count integration and full-range fallbacks make coverage uniform at every sample size. The critical likelihood identity preserves censor information; the open modulus question asks how much can be gained beyond rate-optimal calibration.
